title: What are NPM and Yarn?
description: Understand the two dominant JavaScript package managers and when to use each.

data.text: NPM (Node Package Manager) and Yarn are the two most widely used package managers for JavaScript and TypeScript. They let you install, update, and manage dependencies in your projects.

A package manager automates the process of installing, upgrading, configuring, and removing software packages from a project. In the JavaScript ecosystem, NPM ships with Node.js by default, while Yarn was created by Facebook to address NPM's early performance and reliability issues.

data.title: Why It Matters
data.text: Choosing the right package manager affects install speed, disk usage, lockfile reliability, and CI/CD performance.
NPM is bundled with Node.js and uses a centralized registry at registry.npmjs.com. It stores metadata in package.json and dependency trees in node_modules.
Yarn introduced Plug'n'Play (PnP), workspaces, and deterministic installs. Modern Yarn (Berry) is backward compatible and optimized for monorepos.

items.question: Which should I use?
items.answer: Both work well. NPM is more common in legacy projects. Yarn often offers faster installs and better workspace support for monorepos.

items.question: Can I switch between them?
items.answer: Yes, but delete the old lockfile and node_modules first to avoid conflicts.

items.text: NPM and Yarn manage JavaScript dependencies.
Both use package.json and a lockfile for reproducibility.
Yarn excels in monorepo and workspace scenarios.
Choose based on team preference and project needs.
